message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today National Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. Over his career, LeBron has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers. He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). Known for his versatility, athleticism, court vision, and leadership, LeBron has been selected to numerous All-Star games and has earned multiple All-NBA and All-Defensive Team honors.

Beyond the court, LeBron is also known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron to support at-risk youth. He has also pursued acting and business ventures, including producing films and television shows, and has become a prominent voice on social issues.
